meetings.title: Maya / Elena 1:1
segments: Hi Elena! How's your week going?
Busy, but good. The webinar last week had four hundred signups, which is our best ever.
And the competitive teardown is done, I'll share it after this.
Did anything surprise you in the questions people asked during the webinar?
Yes. Almost half the questions were about trust.
'How do I know the AI is right', 'can I see which comments it used.'
Nobody asked about features. They asked whether they could believe it.
That's really important. It matches what Priya keeps saying about showing the underlying comments.
I'd like the launch messaging to lean into that.
Traceability as a feature, not a footnote.
Four hundred, that's great. Congratulations. What drove it?
Honestly, the title. We called it 'Stop reading every support ticket,' and people clicked.
It tells me the problem framing resonates more than feature names.
That's a really useful insight for Insights 2.0 messaging.
That's actually my main worry.
I'm hearing about Insights 2.0 in pieces.
A design screenshot here, a Slack thread there.
I don't know the scope or the timing, and I'm supposed to be planning a launch.
What would help you most, day to day, beyond the alignment meeting?
A single place where the current scope lives.
Even a simple doc that says what's in, what's out, and when it changes.
Right now I piece it together from Slack.
Fair. I'll make sure the outcome of the alignment meeting becomes that doc, and I'll keep it current.
That's completely fair, and that's on me.
We're having a cross-functional alignment meeting next week to lock scope, the beta, and the SSO question.
I want you there with a slot on the agenda for the launch plan.
Who else is going to be in the alignment meeting?
Raj, Priya, Marcus, Tom, Aisha, and Daniel.
Eight of us. It's a big group, so I'll keep the agenda tight.
You'll have about ten minutes for launch, near the end.
Ten minutes is enough if the one-pager is good. I'll make it good.
Yes, please. That's exactly what I need.
I'll draft a one-page launch plan before that meeting, so there's something concrete to react to.
What do you think goes into the one-pager?
Audience, phases, the core message, what we need from each team, and a rough sequence.
No dates, just the order of things.
And one line on how we'll know it worked.
Perfect. And the 'how we'll know it worked' line is the one people usually forget.
Perfect. What else is on your plate?
The conference booth next month.
It's a lot of logistics, and it's eating into launch prep.
I don't think I can do both well.
How much of the booth work could Ivy take, realistically?
Most of it. Shipping the booth, the printed materials, the schedule for who staffs it.
I'd still want to write the one-line message on the booth, but the logistics are what's eating my time.
Then that's the split. You write the message, Ivy runs the logistics.
Let's not have you do both.
Can we bring in Ivy, the contractor you worked with on the website, for the booth logistics? I'll approve the budget.
That would help enormously. I'll reach out to Ivy this week.
And how are you doing, generally? Not just work.
Honestly, a bit tired. The time zone makes the evenings long, with calls until eight or nine.
But this conversation helps. Knowing the booth is covered takes a lot off my mind.
Let's try to keep your meetings before six your time where we can.
I'll move our 1:1 earlier too.
That would be lovely. Thank you.
Can I give you one piece of feedback on the positioning drafts?
Of course.
They're strong, but they're long, and they lead with what we built.
The webinar just proved people respond to the problem.
I'd lead with a customer's words, and get to the product in the second paragraph.
Can I ask for feedback in the other direction?
When you review my drafts, the comments sometimes come in over several days.
It's hard to know when I have everything.
That's completely fair. I'll do reviews in one pass from now on, and tell you when I'm done.
If I think of something later, I'll flag it as optional.
That would help a lot. Thank you.
Could you share the next draft as a one-pager first, before the full version?
Then I can give direction early, before you've put in all the work.
Yes, that's a good idea.
It would also save me from polishing sections that end up being cut.
Exactly. Direction first, polish later.
I'll try it with the Insights positioning next week.
That's fair. I've been writing for the product team, not for the buyer. I'll rework them.
And longer term, what do you want to be doing more of?
Customer research. I'd love to own a proper research program, especially for naming and positioning.
Right now we guess, then argue about it.
What would a research program look like in your head?
Small to start. A standing panel of ten or fifteen customers we can talk to every month.
Some interviews, some quick surveys, and a shared notes repository, so product, design and marketing all hear the same things.
How would you recruit the panel?
Start with the design partners, then ask Tom's team for a few customers who give great feedback in support conversations.
People who already like telling us things are the best research participants.
Love it. Let's talk about it again in two weeks.
Sounds good. Thanks, Maya.
And this app would be a pretty good place to keep those interview recordings.
Ha, yes. We should use our own product.
I love that. Let's start small.
Use the Insights 2.0 beta as your first research program.
Talk to design partners about what they call things and what they'd pay for.
Should I pitch the research program formally, or just start?
Just start, with the beta.
After two months, write up what you learned and what it would take to make it permanent.
It's much easier to get budget for something that's already working.
That's great advice. Thank you, Maya.
That's a great first project. Thank you.
